## Summary

The fix is a one-line change in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:102`: `destroy()` was deleting posts without ever calling `this.authorize('delete', [Post, post])`, even though `PostPolicy.delete()` (which restricts deletion to the post's author) already existed and was already used correctly by `update()`/`edit()` — it just wasn't wired into `destroy()`. Adding that one `authorize` call closes the gap: a signed-in non-author now gets a 403 and the post survives, a guest gets the normal auth-middleware redirect, and the author can still delete their own posts.

I also added a `posts.destroy` test suite in `tests/PostController.test.ts` covering all three cases (non-author forbidden, unauthenticated refused, author succeeds), using `resetDatabase()` between tests since this suite needs real users/posts in the SQLite test DB.
